title: Zipf's Law: Why the Same Strange Pattern Shows Up Everywhere
question: Why does the same simple mathematical relationship — where the most common item is twice as frequent as the second, three times as frequent as the third, and so on — appear in word frequencies, city sizes, earthquake magnitudes, and internet traffic alike?
summary: Across wildly different domains — language, cities, wealth, websites, even the notes in a piece of music — the frequency of an item is often inversely proportional to its rank. This near-universal pattern, called Zipf's Law, has no single agreed-upon explanation, despite being one of the most robust empirical regularities in complex systems.
